title: How to Get Four People Across a Bridge Before the Torch Dies
request: this is a thriller script make a video for this one you must use the dark background sounds we created the thriller ones

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: If the slowest person holds everyone back, who should walk with them?

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The smart plan fails. Watch.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Four people must cross this rope bridge before the storm breaks it.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Two fit at a time, and someone must carry the torch back each time.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The man in the red tie crosses in one minute, and the woman in the scarf in two.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The woman with the bag needs five, the old man ten.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Two together walk at the slower pace.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: And the torch will last *seventeen* minutes.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: You're fastest. Walk us over one at a time.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Ten, five and two minutes, plus two runs back, makes *nineteen* minutes.

lines.speaker: cheat
lines.text: The torch only lasts seventeen minutes.

lines.speaker: cheat
lines.text: So we leave the old man. Without him, we make it easily.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Nobody stays behind.

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Every trip with the old man takes ten minutes, whoever walks beside him.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: So who should walk beside the old man?

lines.speaker: saint
lines.text: Put the two slow ones together, and we only wait once.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The two fastest cross in two minutes. The man in the red tie runs back in one.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Then the two slowest cross *together*, in ten.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The woman in the scarf returns in two, and the two fastest cross again in two.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: That is exactly *seventeen* minutes.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The old man's ten minutes were coming anyway, so the five fit inside them.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: This is a real puzzle. Saul Levmore and Elizabeth Cook printed it in a book in 1981.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: In 2002, the mathematician Günter Rote proved the fastest way for any group.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: You make the first plan every time you spread slow jobs across your day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Start your slowest jobs at the same time, so you only wait once.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: So who should walk with the slowest person? The next slowest *one*.

sources: Saul X. Levmore and Elizabeth Early Cook, Super Strategies for Puzzles and Games, Doubleday, 1981. The earliest known printed version of the bridge puzzle: four people, one light, a bridge that holds two at a time. As given in Biku's script.

Günter Rote, "Crossing the Bridge at Night", Bulletin of the EATCS, No. 78, October 2002, pages 241 to 246. Solves the puzzle for any number of people with any walking times. https://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/rote/Papers/abstract/Crossing+the+bridge+at+night.html

Checked by Claude on 2026-10-15: with crossing times of 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes, the fastest walking each one over takes 10 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 2 = 19 minutes; the two fastest over, the fastest back, the two slowest over together, the second fastest back, the two fastest over takes 2 + 1 + 10 + 2 + 2 = 17. What the scene invents: the gorge, the storm, the people.
